newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's "Paca the witch" held over Salinas mystery.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's "Paca the witch" held over Salinas mystery.

text.p: "Paca," a witch or soothsayer caught up in a high-drama political murder mystery, was ordered under house arrest by Mexican officials on Tuesday while they continued their investigations.
The woman allegedly led investigators last year to the ranch of Raul Salinas, brother of ex-president Carlos Salinas, where a body was dug up that police at the time alleged Raul had murdered.

Insisting that the corpse was planted, a new team of investigators said they were now keen to interrogate Paca, her sister and Raul's ex-lover Maria Bernal -- all of whom had been involved in the corpse's discovery.
"We're going to seek house arrest," Mexico City Attorney General Jose Gonzalez told reporters. Television stations reported the three women had been confined to their homes.
The detentions marked the latest stage in the unravelling of a bungled case against Raul Salinas that led to the firing in December of Attorney General Antonio Lozano Gracia.
He had pursued the theory that Raul murdered a colleague, Congressman Manuel Munoz Rocha, after the two men masterminded the September 1994 murder of a top ruling party politician.

The corpse in Raul's garden was at first believed to be that of Munoz Rocha, but after Lozano Gracia was fired, investigators rejected that theory. Munoz Rocha has not been seen or heard from for more than two years. Raul Salinas is in jail on murder charges.
Gonzalez said there were no current plans to interrogate Pablo Chapa Benzanilla, the former special prosecutor who officials speculated may have paid Paca to implicate Raul in Munoz Rocha's murder.

Besides detaining Paca, whose real name is Francisca Zetina, Gonzalez said police were also hunting for Ramiro Aguilar Lucero, a "secret witness" who apparently told Chapa Benzanilla he saw Salinas bludgeon Munoz Rocha to death with a bat at his ranch.
